ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A table tennis table with a table tennis ball launcher is shown in Figure 5. The launcher is installed at the midpoint of the left edge of the tabletop, and can horizontally launch identical table tennis balls at different speeds toward different directions on the right side. Table tennis ball 1 lands at the midpoint on the edge of the tabletop on the right side of the net, and table tennis ball 2 lands at a certain point near the midpoint on the edge of the tabletop on the right side of the net. Neglect air resistance. Then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When landing on the table, the powers of the work done by gravity on table tennis ball 1 and table tennis ball 2 are equal

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A table tennis table with a table tennis ball launcher is shown in Figure 5. The launcher is installed at the midpoint of the left edge of the tabletop, and can horizontally launch identical table tennis balls at different speeds toward different directions on the right side. Table tennis ball 1 lands at the midpoint on the edge of the tabletop on the right side of the net, and table tennis ball 2 lands at a certain point near the midpoint on the edge of the tabletop on the right side of the net. Neglect air resistance. When landing on the table, what is the relationship between the powers of the work done by gravity on table tennis ball 1 and table tennis ball 2?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When landing on the table, the powers of the work done by gravity on table tennis ball 1 and table tennis ball 2 are equal
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Near the edge of the tabletop on the left side of the figure is labeled “launch point”; two dashed trajectories are drawn to the right from the same launch point; in the middle there is a net labeled “net”; after crossing the net, the two trajectories respectively land near the edge of the tabletop on the right side, and the landing points are marked with 1 and 2. Although the horizontal motion directions and landing positions of the two balls are different, the landing points in the figure are both at the same tabletop height of the same table tennis table. Reasoning: The stem states that the two balls are identical table tennis balls, launched horizontally from the same launcher, and air resistance is neglected. Therefore both balls can be regarded as projectile motions from the same height with initial vertical velocity 0. The magnitude and direction of the horizontal velocity only affect the horizontal displacement and do not affect the vertical motion. The two balls fall from the same initial height to the same tabletop height, so the vertical falling height is the same, and therefore the vertical velocity components at the instant of landing on the table are the same. The instantaneous power of the work done by gravity is P=\vec{G}\cdot\vec{v}=mgv_y (taking the downward component), and the two balls have the same mass and the same v_y when landing on the table, so the powers of the work done by gravity are equal.
